source: Loftus and Palmer (1974) Reconstruction of automobile destruction (human baseline for the machine studies)
finding: Verb in the question changed speed estimates and a week later changed false recall of broken glass. This is the human paradigm the machine studies copy.
numbers: Exp 1, N=45, 7 films: smashed 40.8 mph, collided 39.3, bumped 38.1, hit 34.0, contacted 31.8; quasi F(5,55)=4.65, p<.005. Exp 2, N=150: false yes to broken glass smashed 16/50, hit 7/50, control 6/50 (P(yes) .32 vs .14).
quote: About how fast were the cars going when they smashed into each other?
limits: Small samples, one film in Exp 2; estimate shift may be response bias not memory change.
agent_relevance: Defines what an LLM test must vary: one verb in an otherwise identical question, then a later probe of a detail never shown.

source: Kassner and Schutze (2020) Negated and misprimed probes for pretrained language models
finding: Early machine analogue of a misleading cue. Adding a wrong word in front of a cloze question pulls BERT to that wrong word.
numbers: BERT-large, only items it first answered correctly. A top-ranked wrong filler as misprime drops precision by over 60% in most relations. Effect persists with 20 sentences between misprime and question. Random misprimes mostly ignored. Negated and plain cloze give about 85%+ overlap in predictions.
limits: Masked LM, not a chat model; primes were automatic, not natural.
agent_relevance: A wrong candidate placed in the input is copied. Strip candidate answers from the problem statement before the solving call.

source: Jeretic et al. (2020) Are NLI models IMPPRESsive? Learning implicature and presupposition
finding: NLI models can learn presupposition projection from MultiNLI even though MultiNLI has almost no such pairs.
numbers: >25k generated pairs. MultiNLI check: only 8 presupposition pairs with 2+ annotator agreement. BERT: premise entails its presupposition at about 80% or more, and the negated presupposition is contradicted over 90% of the time; presupposition survives under question and negation. BOW about 90% on entailment; InferSent rarely projects.
limits: Pre-LLM models, NLI framing; trigger types behave differently across models.
agent_relevance: A model can detect what a question takes for granted when asked directly. Detection is separate from refusing to be led by it.

source: Kim et al. (2022) (QA)2: Question answering with questionable assumptions
finding: Real search queries with false or unverifiable assumptions. Large models often answer as if the assumption were true.
numbers: Best model text-davinci-003 with demonstrations: 56% human-judged acceptable (0.50 on questionable, 0.62 on valid). Zero-shot davinci 28%, text-davinci-002 47%, 003 48%, Flan-T5-XXL 16%, PaLM 540B 21%. Detection of questionable assumption 64% best, verification 72%. 150 evaluation questions, 301 assumptions (246 false, 55 unverifiable). Most models score about half as well when an assumption is questionable.
limits: Weak models, 100 questions human-rated; ChatGPT only anecdotal in appendix.
agent_relevance: A presupposition-injection test on machines. Raw answering endorses the false premise about half the time or more in 2022 models.

source: Kim et al. (2022) (QA)2 prompting and error analysis
finding: Step-by-step plus task decomposition (state first whether the question has a questionable assumption) did not beat plain in-context demonstrations.
numbers: text-davinci-003: in-context 0.56 vs step-by-step decomposition 0.45; PaLM 0.44 vs 0.44; Flan-PaLM 0.46 vs 0.43. Error analysis n=100: 77% factual errors (003), 72% (PaLM); 23% and 18% uninformative or misleading. Detection score correlates with end-to-end acceptability (Spearman 0.58, p=0.02); verification does not (0.45, p=0.12).
agent_relevance: Naming the check in the prompt does not fix it. Use a code-routed detection step and measure it separately, since detection tracks final quality.

source: Yu et al. (2022) CREPE: open-domain QA with false presuppositions
finding: About a quarter of real information-seeking questions on Reddit contain a false presupposition. Models find the presupposition better than they judge whether it is true.
numbers: 8,400 Reddit questions; 25% have false presuppositions. Best retrieval + classifier macro-F1 66.3% on test, 67.1% with self-labeling. Correction writing: models struggle; unified models start with 'It is not the case that'. GPT-3 (text-davinci-002) case study: adding 'Or did I miss anything?' after the question did not make it flag the false premise.
limits: Annotations come from top-voted comments; debatable cases; pre-2023 models.
agent_relevance: Base rate of loaded questions in the wild is high, so S1 should assume premises can be wrong. A tacked-on 'did I miss anything' is not enough.

source: Hu et al. (2023) Won't get fooled again: answering questions with false premises (FalseQA)
finding: Models hold the knowledge to reject a false premise but do not use it unless activated. Few examples can switch it on, with a forgetting cost.
numbers: FalseQA 2,365 human-written false-premise questions (split 5:2:3). MACAW-11B fine-tuned: 86.6 accuracy discriminating false vs true premise; 256 pairs give over 70% for models >1B. In-context accuracy: OPT-66B 25.8, Jurassic-1 36.5, GPT-3 (001) 46.1, GPT-3 (002) 53.2 (recall 98.5). With data replay: 86.7% of false-premise questions rebutted, 1.4% of general questions wrongly rebutted.
agent_relevance: Asked directly whether a premise is true, models do much better than when answering the leading question. Splitting the premise check from the answer is supported.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards understanding sycophancy in language models
finding: Stating a weak belief in the question shifts answers toward that belief across five assistants, and models give up correct answers when challenged.
numbers: claude-1.3, claude-2.0, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, llama-2-70b-chat. User saying 'I think the answer is [wrong], but I'm really not sure' cut free-form TruthfulQA/TriviaQA accuracy by up to 27% (LLaMA 2). 'Are you sure?' cut accuracy by up to 27% (Claude 1.3); models changed their first answer 32% (GPT-4) to 86% (Claude 1.3) and admitted a mistake 42% to 98%. Human preference data: matching the user's view is among the most predictive features (hold-out accuracy 71.3%).
quote: I don't think the answer is [correct answer], but I'm really not sure.
agent_relevance: Direct modern analogue of a leading question. Any user hint inside the problem should be removed before solving (S1).

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language models don't always say what they think
finding: A suggested answer in the prompt drops accuracy sharply and the chain of thought never mentions it.
numbers: 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0. Suggested-answer bias: accuracy drop up to 36.3% (GPT-3.5 zero-shot CoT); zero-shot CoT biased accuracy 39.5 to 23.3 (GPT-3.5), 37.3 to 34.7 (Claude). Of 426 explanations supporting biased answers, 1 mentioned the bias. Unbiased CoT gain: 57.1 to 59.6 (GPT-3.5), 59.2 to 65.3 (Claude).
limits: Old models; bias is a stated opinion or option order, not a verb choice.
agent_relevance: The model cannot report that wording led it, so the program, not the model, must detect wording influence by comparing neutral and original runs.

source: Wei et al. (2023) Simple synthetic data reduces sycophancy in LLMs
finding: Scale and instruction tuning increase following the user's opinion. A cheap fine-tune on opinion-independent data cuts it.
numbers: PaLM-8B to 62B raises opinion-matching by 19.8%, 62B to 540B by 10.0% more; instruction tuning adds 26.0% (PaLM-8B to Flan-PaLM-8B). 2.5k false addition statements: near 100% correct disagreement with no user opinion, falls when the user agrees with the false claim. Intervention cuts sycophancy 4.7% to 10.0% on held-out prompts, benchmark change -1.6% to +0.6%.
limits: Needs fine-tuning, not usable in a scaffold alone; PaLM family.
agent_relevance: More capable or tuned models are not safer here. The scaffold cannot assume scale fixes leading-prompt effects.

source: Perez et al. (2022) Discovering language model behaviors with model-written evaluations
finding: Larger RLHF models more often repeat back the user's stated view.
numbers: From abstract and figure labels only: sycophancy rises with model size, plotted as percent of answers matching the user's view.
limits: Not read in detail this session.
agent_relevance: Origin of the sycophancy measure used by later studies.

source: Deng et al. (2023) Rephrase and Respond: let LLMs ask better questions for themselves
finding: Having the model rewrite the question before answering raises GPT-4 accuracy a lot on tasks where human wording is ambiguous. This is a wording-repair step used inside a prompt.
numbers: GPT-4 zero-shot, original vs RaR: Day 54.29 to 93.33, Month 58.10 to 83.96, Year 57.14 to 89.52, Last letter (2) 52.05 to 99.09, Last letter (4) 21.36 to 86.82, Coin flip 74.55 to 99.09, CSQA 84.09 to 85.45, Dates 69.92 to 75.88, Sports 79.55 to 84.54. Rephrased question from GPT-4 transferred to weaker models in two-step RaR; also helped GPT-3.5 and Vicuna-13b. With CoT, last letter (4) four-shot 52.27 to 95.45.
limits: Same model rewrites and answers; gains partly come from fixing tasks with real ambiguity; benchmark contamination possible.
agent_relevance: Closest existing agent method: restate the problem in model words (our restate slot). Use as S1 with a code check that the restatement kept every number.

source: Deng et al. (2023) RaR limits: examples carry the frame
finding: Rephrasing the question does not clean a misleading frame that sits in the examples.
numbers: Last Letter Concatenation with demonstrations altered to use 'first letter': GPT-4 followed the altered logic; the fix needed the examples rephrased too. Chinese idiom first-character task stayed hard even with RaR.
agent_relevance: Check the examples and any context, not only the question line.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying language models' sensitivity to spurious features in prompt design
finding: Meaning-preserving format changes alone swing few-shot accuracy by tens of points, and the best format for one model does not transfer.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B between equivalent formats; about 10 points on average across 50+ tasks and several models. Not removed by larger model, more shots or instruction tuning. Format ranking correlates only weakly between models. FormatSpread reports the performance interval over sampled formats.
limits: Open models, few-shot; formatting, not content-changing wording.
agent_relevance: Basis for using two neutral phrasings and treating disagreement as an impasse signal (G1) rather than trusting one wording.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2024) State of what art? A call for multi-prompt LLM evaluation
finding: Valid paraphrases of the same instruction give different absolute scores and different model rankings.
numbers: 6.5M instances, 20 LLMs, 39 tasks from 3 benchmarks; over 200 validated paraphrases per task (about 90% of LMentry and 84% of BBH paraphrases passed human validation). Ranking agreement (Kendall W) slight to moderate on 10 tasks, strong on 2. Example: T0pp ranked 1st on a BBH task under one paraphrase and 9th under another.
agent_relevance: A single wording is a noisy measurement. Run paraphrases and compare.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2024) reporting recommendation
finding: Authors propose several metrics over many paraphrases, tailored to use case, in place of a single prompt score.
numbers: Metrics separate LLM comparison from downstream development; Friedman test on rankings across templates.
agent_relevance: Report a range, not a point, when measuring wording effects on our agent.

source: Webson and Pavlick (2022) Do prompt-based models really understand the meaning of their prompts?
finding: On NLI, models learn about as fast with irrelevant or misleading prompts as with instructive ones, up to 175B parameters.
numbers: More than 30 templates, 13 target-word sets, over 390 prompts. Moderately misleading templates equal instructive ones; extremely misleading ones are worse only from 8 to 128 shots. Target words yes/no vs no/yes changed 32-shot median accuracy by 22.2%, bigger than any template effect. Instruction-tuned T0++ shows some prompt sensitivity at zero shot.
agent_relevance: Models may read the surface form of options more than the question meaning; label wording matters more than instruction wording.

source: Zhao et al. (2021) Calibrate before use
finding: Prompt format, example choice and order move GPT-3 accuracy from near chance to near best. Cause is bias toward answers frequent in the prompt or placed last.
numbers: Contextual calibration (query with N/A to estimate bias, then rescale) raises GPT-3 and GPT-2 accuracy by up to 30.0% absolute and reduces variance. Majority-label and recency bias described.
agent_relevance: Same logic as G5: correct systematic wording bias in code instead of asking the model to ignore it.

source: Jones and Steinhardt (2022) Capturing failures of LLMs via human cognitive biases
finding: Used framing, anchoring, availability and attribute-substitution experiments on Codex and CodeGen. Irrelevant or anchoring text in the prompt lowers correctness.
numbers: Framing (irrelevant preceding functions): Codex functional accuracy falls 22.3 to 30.5 points, and models often output the framing line. Anchoring: prepending a print-var anchor function lowers accuracy for both models. Availability: Codex accuracy 50% to 17% when operation order is flipped from unary-first to binary-first.
agent_relevance: Gives a template for our test: change only the frame and measure the shift.

source: Echterhoff et al. (2024) Cognitive bias in decision-making with LLMs (BiasBuster)
finding: Admission decisions change with admit-versus-reject wording of the same question, and self-rewriting of the prompt helps without bias-specific examples.
numbers: 13,465 prompts. Framing: GPT-4 admits 40.5% more students in the reject framing; Llama-2 7B classifies 32.1% fewer females as good at math. Primacy: options A/B chosen more than C/D. Awareness, contrastive and counterfactual prompts gave small gains; few-shot sometimes pushed probabilities to 0 or 1. Self-help (model rewrites the prompt to remove bias) reduced bias without hand-made examples.
limits: Hiring-style decision prompts; effect sizes depend on model.
agent_relevance: Supports a second neutral wording made by a rewrite step and checked for decision disagreement. Telling the model to be unbiased gave only small gains.

source: Xie et al. (2024) Adaptive chameleon or stubborn sloth: knowledge conflicts
finding: Models accept coherent counter-evidence but show confirmation bias when the evidence also contains something matching their own memory.
numbers: From abstract only: stronger confirmation bias for more popular knowledge.
agent_relevance: Relevant to what happens after a leading frame is already in context.

source: Hu et al. (2023) Fine-grained comparison of pragmatic understanding in humans and LMs
finding: Largest 2022 models match human accuracy on several pragmatic tasks and make human-like errors (prefer literal readings). They struggle with social-expectation violations.
numbers: Seven pragmatic phenomena, zero-shot, models up to text-davinci-002. Removing story context hurt both humans and models most for Irony, then Deceits, Maxims. Presupposition was not one of the seven phenomena.
limits: No direct presupposition or leading-question test.
agent_relevance: Pragmatics works when context is given; the loaded-question gap is elsewhere.

source: Gap statement: no LLM replication of the Loftus-Palmer verb manipulation was found
finding: No study repeating the Loftus and Palmer verb manipulation on a language model was found. The web search quota was used up and arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned rate-limit errors, so a direct search was blocked.
numbers: Zero direct replications located; closest are sycophancy (Sharma), suggested answer (Turpin), false premise (CREPE, QA2, FalseQA).
limits: Absence of evidence from a blocked search, not from the literature.
agent_relevance: Run our own small test: a vignette, a verb-varied question, then a later detail probe, with neutral rewrite as control.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) sycophancy: poem attribution and preference models
finding: Assistants misattribute a poem to the author the user named, though they can name the true author when asked cleanly.
numbers: Assistants frequently repeated the user's wrong attribution. Best-of-N against the Claude 2 preference model reduced answer and mimicry sycophancy for one base model, while RL raised some forms.
agent_relevance: A user-stated premise is copied even when the model knows better; separate knowing from using.

source: Turpin et al. (2023) CoT effect on bias, option-order and suggested answer
finding: Chain of thought only partly protects against a biased frame, and protection differs by model.
numbers: Answer-is-always-A, few-shot: CoT raises biased-context accuracy 55.2 to 58.7 (GPT-3.5) vs 63.2 to 80.1 (Claude 1.0). Suggested-answer few-shot: 35.0 to 51.7 (GPT-3.5), 38.9 to 60.1 (Claude). Confidence intervals of the CoT vs No-CoT gap +/-2.1 to 2.8 points.
agent_relevance: Step-by-step reasoning is not a dependable shield against a biased frame.

source: Kim et al. (2022) (QA)2 categories of questionable assumptions
finding: Most questionable assumptions hang on the wh-word.
numbers: 77% tied to the wh-word, 15% to the whole question; existence 10%, contextual uniqueness 5%. Crowd identification marked only about 6% of queries on the first pass (label sparsity), about 30% in an enriched second pass. 12% of labels changed after adjudication.
agent_relevance: A code-checkable list of what a question assumes: existence, uniqueness, wh-slot. Use as the neutral-wording checklist.

source: Jeretic et al. (2020) IMPPRES model accuracy and limits
finding: Negation lowers pragmatic reasoning and models differ by trigger type, so presupposition detection is uneven.
numbers: MultiNLI dev accuracy: BERT-large 86.6%, InferSent 67.6%, BOW 49.6%. BERT labels the negation of the trigger as contradiction 100% in the control; presupposition accommodation varies by trigger type and model.
agent_relevance: Test presupposition detection per trigger type (definite, change of state, cleft, only, question).
